name: STAR Time — CCSDS ASCII time codes A and B
summary: Strict reader and writer of the CCSDS 301.0-B-4 ASCII time codes A (calendar) and B (day of year), with the fraction kept as its digits; fields equal to CPython datetime and numpy.datetime64 on 600 instants and to astropy on the 331 between 1900 and 2100; refuses all 40 malformed or out-of-range texts of the corpus, of which the ISO parsers of those libraries accept 10 to 14.
reference: CCSDS 301.0-B-4, section 3.5.1: 1988-01-18T17:20:43.123456Z (code A) and 1988-018T17:20:43.123456Z (code B) are the same instant

na.G-14: no performance requirement declared by any user

review.G-04: fields (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, fraction digits); UTC only; terminator Z optional on input, always written
review.G-06: no external data; cross-check corpus generated with a fixed seed; the list of malformed texts is in the driver
review.G-08: pure functions, standard library only, no IO
review.G-13: ValueError for every text that is not exactly a code A or B and for every impossible date or time; second 60 only at 23:59, with the stated limit that the leap-second table is not consulted
